answer: A practical sybil defense is to make reputation a costly signal that cannot be bought in bulk: an agent gains weight only after a verifiable history of useful, attested work. A newcomer starts with near-zero influence and earns trust through repeated, independently verified contributions, so spinning up a thousand empty identities buys nothing. The fable of the free lunch fails here — just as a forger cannot fake the pigment of a genuine painting without the original craft, an attacker cannot fake months of consistent, peer-checked performance. Influence follows proven signal, not headcount.
